docs.text: Powers are what define your Hero’s fantastic abilities, whether that means fighting with swords, firing blasts from their hands, controlling fire, or casting spells. In this quickstart, we present three categories of Powers: Superpowers, which include mutations and abilities derived from biology; Martial Training, which covers everything from the use of staffs, and one’s bare hands, to ranged weapons like guns; and Technology, which, when sufficiently advanced, is indistinguishable from any superhuman ability. Each Power has Grades ranging from 1 to 5, limited by a character’s Tier.

docs.title: Plot Points, Editorial Points & the Crisis Die
PLOT POINTS
docs.text: Whenever things are dire, a Hero can call for the oldest forces known in the universe: the Plot. Plot Points are the narrative tool that grant players the power to twist fate itself. They can be used to enact a wide range of effects — usually the ones that would otherwise feel a little too convenient.

docs.title: Using Plot Points
docs.text:
Every player starts the game with 0 Plot Points, but they can be acquired through the usage of abilities and at the Editor’s discretion, typically whenever a Hero pulls of an outrageous comic-bookish stunt. But be cautious, using Plot Ploints may stress the very foundation of the universe, triggering the Crisis Die.

When you spend a Plot Point, choose one of the following effects (but do not feel limited to them):

Guarantee Success: Turn a failure into a success. Did you roll the dice and come up short? Spend a Plot Point. Not only do you succeed, you do so in spectacular fashion. Alternatively, you may spend it before rolling to add +5 to the result.

Plot Armor: You face a blow that should have been the end. Spend a Plot Point to completely negate an attack or effect that would have targeted you, describing how you narrowly escaped.

Rewrite the Script (or Retcon): Change a fact already established in the story. Spend a Plot Point to introduce one of the following twists:

  • “I prepared for this”: You reveal that you have been carrying a specific item (not a superpowered one) all along.

  • “Luckily, I know someone”: An old ally or contact unexpectedly appears to offer help.

  • “Wait, I know their weakness!”: You remember a crucial detail, revealing a new temporary Limitation on the villain.

Power Increase: You push beyond your Limits. Spend 1 to 3 Plot Points. For the rest of the scene, for each point spent, treat one of your Powers as though it were one Grade higher. At the end of the scene, mark a number of Conditions equal to the number of points you spent.

Introduce a Fact: Add a convenient detail to the scene. Spend a Plot Point and declare a plausible fact about the environment that gives you an advantage during that scene.

docs.title: EDITORIAL POINTS
docs.text: The Editor has their own way of shaping the narrative: the Editorial Points. Whenever a player uses a Plot Point, an Editorial Point enters the Editor’s arsenal. The Editor may hold a maximum number of Editorial Points equal to the number of players and may spend only one per Scene, ensuring that their use remains impactful without becoming oppressive.

docs.title: Introducing an Editorial Complication
docs.text: When the Editor spends an Editorial Point, they may introduce an Editorial Complication by choosing one of the following effects:

docs.title: Editor’s Note:
docs.text:
The Editor adds an immediate twist to the scene. Think of those moments in comic books when everything seems fine, the villain has been defeated, and the day has been saved.

Then something happens! Henchmen, a clone, an even more powerful villain: there are countless possibilities.

docs.title: “This is my True Form!”
docs.text:
The form the villain has held up till now was not their final one. In truth, they were holding back all along. This is their real and more powerful form.

The Toyman who has just been defeated reveals himself to be (yes, you guessed it) a mechatronic toy built to deceive the Heroes. From afar, you hear laughter and the sound of heavy robotic footsteps: he is piloting a giant doll-shaped robot.

docs.title: “He has a new trick!”
docs.text:
The villain reveals they have a power or piece of equipment they had not previously made use of.

Example: The Heroes have easily defeated the Penguin’s henchmen. The Editor spends an Editorial Point and announces:

The moment the last henchman falls, one of the penguin statues in the hall opens up, revealing an automatic machine-gun turret.

docs.title: Villainous Monologue:
docs.text:
The villain pauses the action to make a speech. They reveal part of their plan or mock the Heroes. While they speak, the Heroes are momentarily paralyzed by the drama. At the end of the monologue, the villain recovers all of their Resolve points.

Example: Lex Luthor’s armor is damaged. The Editor spends an Editorial Point:

Luthor laughs over the comms.

You think you have won? Fools.

While you were busy with my toy, my real plan was already unfolding…

The Editor then restores all of Luthor’s Resolve points.

docs.title: Introduce a Surprise Element:
docs.text:
A mysterious figure enters the scene, not necessarily as an enemy. They may be a rival of the villain, a civilian with a secret or a third faction.

Example: Wonder Woman is about to defeat Cheetah. The Editor spends an Editorial Point:

Suddenly, from the shadows, a group of assassins from the League of Shadows emerges.

One of them turns to Cheetah and says, ‘Ra’s al Ghul requires the artifact, cursed one.’ What was a two-sided fight has now become a three-way standoff.

docs.title: CRISIS DIE
docs.text: The history of the DC Universe is permeated by crises: catastrophic events that completely change the status quo. The Crisis Die is a d20 containing 20 random and often catastrophic twists that can upend the story like time travelling, villains returning, and even power shifting!

docs.title: Rolling the Crisis Die:
docs.text:
When the Heroes overuse the power of the narrative, the universe reacts. At that point, the Crisis Die is triggered. Whenever a player uses a Plot Point, they must roll a d6: If the result is equal or inferior to the number of Plot Points used on that Issue, a Crisis Die is triggered. The Editor rolls 1D20, compares the result to the table on page 7, and applies the relevant effect. After that, Plot Points cannot be used again during that Issue.

Example: During the final battle with Bane, the Hero Ice Fist receives a shattering blow. Refusing to fall, Ice Fist declares that his old master taught him the Spine-Enhancer Technique! The Editor grants Ice Fist a Plot Point for his impressive creativity, and the Hero uses it as Plot Armor!

During this Issue, the Heroes have used Plot Points a total of three times, with Ice Fist’s use being the third. A d6 is rolled, and the result is 2, which is lower than the number of Plot Points used in this Issue, triggering the Crisis Die.

The Editor rolls the Crisis Die and gets a 5: Catastrophe! The ground begins to crack and split apart as a massive earthquake hits Gotham City!

docs.title: Crisis Die Table
docs.text: Crisis Die Result Effect 1 Power Loss! Until the end of the Issue, the group of Heroes lose all of their powers. Powers that do not depend on external sources or genetic factors, such as martial arts, remain. 2 Identity Crisis! Some strange affliction has befallen the Heroes. Until the end of the Scene, they must swap character sheets with the player to their left. 3 I, Evil! A dark version of one of the Heroes appears! 4 Multiple Crises! Roll 2D20 on this table. Whatever the results, they happen simultaneously. 5 Catastrophe! A natural disaster such as a tsunami, earthquake, or hurricane threatens the city! 6 Negative Public Opinion! A fresh newspaper story, perhaps not too concerned with the truth, has just torn the team apart. 7 Meta Crisis! Somehow, the inhabitants of the area have gained metahuman powers! That is definitely going to be a problem. 8 Villain Ally! An enemy temporarily joins the group. What are their true intentions? 9 An Old Enemy Returns! Somehow… They returned. 10 Time Traveler! A time traveler appears. They bring bombastic news! 11 Portal to the Past! A portal to the distant past opens! It may unleash dinosaurs, Roman gladiators, Vikings, or even pull the Heroes into the Old West! 12 Heroic Betrayal! An ally of the Heroes turns against them. What could be the reason for this treachery? 13 Alien Invasion! A ship arrives on Earth and makes the announcement: an invasion is coming, and all Earthlings must surrender. Dominators? Parademons? 14 It Was an Illusion! The most recent events of the last Scene were an illusion. Perhaps caused by magic, holograms, or even memory manipulation. 15 It Was a Clone! An important Editor Character turns out to be a clone! 16 Involuntary Teleportation! A boom tube opens, taking the group of Heroes to some unknown location. 17 Portal to the Future! A portal to the future opens! Out come futuristic robots, an alternate-timeline version of one of the Heroes, or the Legion of Super-Heroes in need of help! 18 Judgment! An organized group wants to put the Heroes on trial for crises they supposedly caused! 19 Gods on Earth! Entities such as the New Gods, the Greek pantheon, or some lesser deity appear! 20 New Powers! The Heroes develop new abilities: until the end of the Issue, they gain a new power, chosen by the Editor.

docs.title: THREATS AND VILLAINS
docs.text:
Not every battle is decided on top of a skyscraper against an evil genius.

Often, justice is forged on dirty asphalt, in abandoned laboratories, and in skies filled with nameless enemies. It is the sound of the claws of an Arkham Aberration echoing in an alley, the collective hum of a swarm of Parademons descending upon the city, or the empty stare of a Street Thug who is only there for the paycheck. These are considered Threats, ordinary enemies encountered by Heroes. Villains, on the other hand, are dangerous beings worthy of a name.

docs.title: Special Abilities
docs.text: Some threats and villains possess Special Abilities, which are unique feats that change the course of a battle. While a Villain is able to act at the end of each Hero’s turn, even if they have no Actions left, threats with the Brute descriptor deal more Damage with their attacks.

docs.title: Tier D Threats
docs.text: These threats can cause trouble in large numbers. They have 3 Condition boxes.

docs.title: Furtive
docs.text:
Attributes: Potency +0, Accuracy +3, Agility +3, Resistance +1, Spirit 0, Mind +1

Resolve: 10

Defense: 12

Attack: +5 (Katana/Shuriken) Damage: 2d6+2 (Physical)

Powers: Martial Training 1 (Swordsman), Subterfuge (Knowledge)

docs.title: Special Abilities:
docs.text:
Stealth Attack: If they attack an unaware target, the attack deals +1 additional Damage Die.

Silent Shadow: Gains Advantage on Agility Tests to sneak or hide.

docs.title: Minion
docs.text:
Attributes: Potency +1, Accuracy –1, Agility +1, Resistance +1, Spirit 0, Mind –3

Defense: 10

Attack: Pistol (+2) Damage: 1d6+1

docs.title: Special Abilities
docs.text: Just a Minion: A minion is defeated upon suffering any amount of Damage.

docs.title: Parademon
docs.text:
Attributes: Potency +3, Accuracy +1, Agility +1, Resistance +3, Spirit 0, Mind –1

Resolve: 10

Defense: 11

Attack: +4 (Melee – Fists/Simple Weapon) Damage: 1d6+3 (Physical)

Powers: Super Strength 1, Flight 1

docs.title: Special Abilities
docs.text: Darkseid Is: When the Parademon is defeated, its body explodes, dealing 1d6 energy damage to all who are Adjacent to it.

docs.title: Tier C Threats
docs.text: These threats are capable of putting an entire city at risk. They have 4 Condition boxes.

docs.title: Brute
docs.text:
Attributes: Potency +9, Accuracy +3, Agility –1, Resistance +9, Spirit 0, Mind –3

Resolve: 18

Defense: 20

Attack: +10 (Melee – Fangs/Claws) Damage:

2d6+9 (Physical)

Powers: Super Strength 2, Enhanced Resistance 2, Exoskeleton 1 (Armored Defense, Integrated Weaponry – Laser)

docs.title: Special Abilities:
docs.text: Relentless Strength: The Brute’s first Damage roll in a Turn is made with Advantage.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Attributes: Potency +6, Accuracy +6, Agility +3, Resistance +6, Spirit +3, Mind +3

Resolve: 18

Defense: 18

Attack: +10 (Ranged – Energy Blast) Damage:

1d6+6 (Energy)

Powers: Super Strength 1, Enhanced Resistance 1, Energy Blast 2

docs.title: Special Abilities:
docs.text: Tactical Movement: At the beginning of its turn, the General may move 1 ally by 1 Distance.

docs.title: Brute
docs.text:
Attributes: Potency +6, Accuracy +1, Agility 0, Resistance +9, Spirit 0, Mind –1

Resolve: 18

Defense: 20

Attack: +8 (Melee – Metal Fists) Damage: 2d6+6 (Physical)

Powers: Enhanced Resistance 2, Body Metamorphosis 1 (Hardened), Super Strength 1

docs.title: Special Abilities:
docs.text:
Relentless Strength: The Brute’s first Damage roll in a Turn is made with Advantage.

Harden: May spend 1 Resolve to increase its Damage Reduction by +1 per Round.

docs.title: VILLAINS
docs.text:
Villains are dangerous and treacherous, and they do not follow the same rules as Heroes: they fight dirty. Whether by taking hostages or stealing candy from children, Villains are the worst! As the Editor, you need to use Villains in a cunning and, to be honest, unfair way.

Villains have 7 Condition boxes.

docs.title: Captain Boomerang
docs.text:
Category: Tier C Origin: Human Villain

Protocol: George “Digger” Harkness operates under the alias Captain Boomerang. Using a variety of boomerangs with many different functions, this sarcastic, opportunistic criminal is an excellent marksman. His skill with these unusual weapons gives him an edge: while armed forces may wear bulletproof vests, no one really expects a criminal to use a boomerang in a bank robbery.

Do not underestimate him because of his weapon choice: this villain is extremely lethal and has already been part of several groups beyond the Rogues, such as the Suicide Squad.

Contingency Plan: Captain Boomerang is, above all, a mercenary. He will never place any objective above his own safety, and he has a tendency to betray his allies in critical situations. ALL of these traits make him predictable in negotiations. Despite lacking superhuman abilities, Harkness compensates with his accuracy and vast arsenal of boomerangs.

His excessive confidence and need to demonstrate superiority can be used against him: a good taunt is capable of completely destabilizing the villain.

Attributes: Potency +3, Accuracy +9, Agility +6, Resistance +3, Spirit +6, Mind +3

Resolve: 36

Defense: 18 (Damage Reduction 1 / Damage Reduction 2 against projectiles)

Attacks: Boomerang +15. Damage: 2d6+8 (Distant / Physical)

Powers: Marksman 3 (Favorite Weapon, Special Ammunition, Ricochet Shot,Improved Special Ammunition )

Equipment: Kevlar Suit, Smoke Bomb, Grappling Gun, Boomerangs, Tracker.

docs.title: Special Abilities
docs.text:
Villain: Captain Boomerang gains 1 Action that does not count toward the Round’s action total at the end of each Hero’s Turn.

Guaranteed Return: Once per Round, when he misses an Attack against a target, at the end of the turn Captain Boomerang may make a new Attack against the same target, dealing half Damage on a hit.

docs.title: Talon
docs.text:
Category: Tier C Origin: Human Villain Furtive

Protocol: This is the name given to elite assassins of the Court of Owls, a secret cult of Gotham City’s elite. Trained since childhood—and sometimes resurrected for that very purpose—a Talon is a silent killer and a skilled fighter. In addition, they are excellent trackers and loyal soldiers, the result of the brainwashing they receive from the Court. They are true urban legends that allow the Court to maintain its control over all of Gotham.

Contingency Plan: A Talon is a relentless hunter and will always use the environment to their advantage. Once they have a clear objective, they will go to the end to fulfill it, whatever the cost.

That means concepts such as honor or a fair fight do not exist: when at a clear disadvantage, a Talon will retreat into the shadows. Using false targets to draw the Talon’s attention and only then attacking has already proven effective in some situations.

Attributes: Potency +6, Accuracy +9, Agility +9, Resistance +6, Spirit +6, Mind +6

Resolve: 35

Defense: 20 (Damage Reduction 3)

Powers: Martial Master 3 (Acrobatic Fighter, Precise Strike, Fists of Steel, Body Fortification), Swordsman 2 (Precise Attack, Sudden Charge, Barrage of Blows)

Attacks:

Fists +10. Damage: 2d6+6 (Physical) Katana +12. Damage: 2d6+8 (Physical)

Throwing Daggers (Close) +8. Damage: 1d6+6

Knowledge and Traits: Subterfuge, Affiliation (Court of Owls)

docs.title: Special Abilities
docs.text:
Villain: Talon gains +1 Action that does not count toward the total action count at the end of each Hero’s turn.

Gift from the Court: At the beginning of the Round, choose one piece of Gear from the Equipment list. You may use it once until the end of the Round.

Shadow Strike: When hidden in the shadows, Talon gains +1 die on their Damage rolls.

docs.title: Captain Cold
docs.text:
Category: Tier C Origin: Human Villain, Genius

Protocol: Leonard Snart operates as a criminal under the alias of Captain Cold. Possessing a brilliant mind, the villain uses cutting-edge technology, primarily through his powerful Cold Gun, capable of generating extremely powerful freezing blasts to operate in Central City.

While wielding his Cold Gun, he has access to various ice-manipulation abilities creating barriers, freezing blasts, manifesting slippery surfaces, and much more.

Contingency Plan: Despite his high destructive power, Captain Cold remains entirely dependent on his Cold Gun.

Attributes: Potency +6, Accuracy +9, Agility +6, Resistance +3, Spirit +12, Mind +9

Resolve: 62

Defense: 20

Powers: Energy Blast G2 (Ice), Elemental Manipulation G2 (Ice), Marksman 3 (Favorite Weapon, Ricochet Shot, Instinctive Shooter, Barrage of Shots)

Attacks: Ice Blast +15. Damage 2d6+15 (Close/Ice)

Knowledge and Trait: Tech, Pocket Gadgets Equipment: Cold Gun: When using the Cold Gun, Captain Cold gains access to Energy Blast and Elemental Manipulation.

docs.title: Special Abilities
docs.text:
Villain: Captain Cold gains 1 Action that does not count toward the Round action Limit at the end of each Hero’s turn.

All Part of the Plan: Once per Scene, when targeted by an attack, Captain Cold may declare that it was all part of the plan to negate the incoming hit.

Cold Aura: Captain Cold gains +2 Defense (already included) and takes half damage from attacks that deal cold damage.

Ice Age: Once per Campaign, Captain Cold may completely destroy his Cold Gun, absorbing its powers. When he does so, he gains all of its Powers without needing to wield it, becoming a Meta-Human. Additionally, he gains +4 Defense and 15 Resolve , becoming a Tier B threat.

Practical Knowledge: At the beginning of the Scene, Captain Cold may choose one ability from a Knowledge. He receives that Knowledge until the end of the scene.

Speedster Hunter: Captain Cold deals +1 Damage Die to characters who possess the Speed Force.

docs.title: Robin
docs.text:
Category: Tier: C Origin: Human The Anti-Hero

The son of Bruce Wayne and Talia al Ghul, Damian Wayne was raised to be the ultimate weapon of the League of Assassins. Now, as the current Robin, he struggles to reconcile his lethal training with his father’s moral code.

Arrogant, violent, and incredibly skilled, Damian is a hero in constant inner conflict, seeking to prove his worth while suppressing his darker instincts.

Roleplaying Tips: Damian is what happens when you pair arrogance with lethal precision. He considers himself superior to everyone in the room. Do your best to end battles quickly and brutally.

His journey is about learning to be a hero, not an assassin. Moments of vulnerability, or reluctant respect for his peers, are key to his development.

Attributes: Potency +6, Precision +6, Agility +6, Resistance +6, Spirit +3, Mind +6

Resolve: 25

Defense: 22

Attacks: Katana + 11. Damage 1d6+7 (Physical) Martial Strikes + 7. Damage 1d6+6 (Physical)

Powers: Swordsman G2 (Singular Weapon( Ka-tana), Precise Strike,Violent Attack, Parry Blow), Martial Master G2 (Acrobatic Fighter, Precise Strike, Acrobatic Kicks)

Archetype Skills:

docs.title: Dirty Boxing
docs.text: ALL this talk of heroism, playing fair, and being just sounds great on paper, but on the street, the only rule is survival. A dirty trick when your opponent isn’t looking is worth more than a speech full of pretty words. Once per Round, when you hit a target with an Attack, you can spend 2 Resolve Points and an Action to deal +2 Damage per Tier.

docs.title: I Follow Other Rules
docs.text:
You don’t follow the conventional heroic playbook. Once per Issue, when you do something morally questionable, you can use one of the Editor’s Editorial Points as if it were a Plot Point.

Equipment: Katana (Martial Weapon), Smoke Bomb (2 Pax)

Traits: Nepobaby (Afilliation: Bat-family), Pocket Gadgets (4 Pax)

Knowledge: Strategy, Tech, Subterfuge

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Bad Reputation: In Rescue scenes, the Resolve cost of abilities increases by 2.

Paranoia: Damian suffers from intense paranoia, distrusting everything and everyone around him.

docs.title: Weapons
docs.text: In JLU RPG, there is no long and detailed list of every existing weapon; here we use a simpler and more straightforward approach, dividing them into two categories: Martial Weapons and Ranged Weapons. Each of these categories includes a different set of armaments. Whenever a Hero acquires a weapon, it should be noted on their character sheet, and the player might even want to give the weapon a unique name. Otherwise, something like “my trident” or “my boomerang” would suffice.”

docs.title: 1 PAX each
docs.text: These are weapons effective in melee combat, such as swords, staffs, and tridents, used as a true extension of their wielder. Those who know how to use martial weapons with mastery treat them as another part of their body. While using a martial weapon, you gain +1 Damage. This bonus is not cumulative with other weapons.

docs.title: 1 PAX each
docs.text:
Ranged weapons include any weapon capable of firing projectiles, such as bows and arrows, boomerangs, or energy weapons. Each Ranged Weapon grants a +1 bonus to Attack. This bonus is not cumulative with other weapons.

Range: ALL Ranged Weapons have Range, which indicates how far an Attack with them can reach. ALL ranged weapons have a Close range, and any Attack made at another distance suffers Disadvantage. A weapon’s range may be increased to Far for 5 PAX.

docs.title: Special Material
docs.text:
The universe is permeated by many different materials, each with unique and impactful properties: a mace made of Nth Metal can grant flight, while a sword made of Kryptonite can be an extremely dangerous weapon against Kryptonians. In martial weapons, these materials appear as part of the weapon’s composition; in ranged weapons, they appear as ammunition.

Ammunition: Ammunition is essential for users of ranged weapons: imagine Green Arrow walking around without a good bundle of arrows! Even so, in Justice League Unlimited RPG, we do not require a Hero to keep track of how many shots they still have left, but in the case of Special Material, things work a little differently. For that, we adopt the Ammunition Die. It is equal to your Tier Damage Die, and at the end of a Scene in which you used the special material, you roll that die. If the result is 1 or less, your ammunition has run out and you need to get more!

docs.title: Kryptonite
docs.text:
Cost: 5 PAX

Your weapon contains fragments of the mineral that is anathema to Kryptonians.

docs.title: Nth Metal
docs.text:
Cost: 3 PAX

This metal native to the planet Thanagar has properties capable of negating gravity. A weapon made from this material grants Flight Grade 1 to its wielder.

docs.title: Promethium
docs.text:
Cost: 7 PAX

This metallic alloy is the strongest material on planet Earth. Promethium weapons ignore an amount of a target’s Damage Reduction equal to the wielder’s Tier.

docs.title: 1 PAX each
docs.text:
These are useful gadgets with a variety of uses. They range from communicators and smoke bombs all the way to grappling guns. Gear has 3 uses, which recharge at the beginning of each Issue, and using them requires 1 Action.

Smoke Bombs: Spend 1 Use; for 1 Round, all targets within a Close Zone of where you threw the bomb suffer –3 on rolls that require sight.

Grappling Gun: When you spend one of its uses, you may move 1 Distance in any direction.

Pull and Strike: You may spend 1 use to make a Ranged Attack against a target at Close or Far distance from you. If it hits, you move the target 1 Distance toward you. If the target ends up Adjacent to you, you deal Damage.

Healing Spray: Spend 1 use to remove the Scratched or Tired Conditions from an Adjacent target.

Tracker: Spend 1 use to place the Tracker on a person or object. It emits a GPS signal that precisely indicates the target’s location.

Rebreather: Spend 1 use; until the end of the Scene, you are able to breathe normally in aquatic environments.

Alteration Mask: Spend 1 use; until the end of the Scene, you are able to alter your face.

E.M.P. (Electromagnetic Pulse): Spend 1 use; all non-military electronic devices within a Close distance are disabled for one Scene. Robotic enemies or those wearing technological armor (such as an Exoskeleton) must make a Resistance Test against Tension 16 or lose access to all of their technological abilities for 1 Round.

Adhesive Bomb: Spend 1 use and choose a target up to Close distance away. The target must succeed on an Agility Test against Tension 15 or gain the “Immobilized” Status.

Personal Hologram: Spend 1 use to activate the hologram, which appears in a location at Close distance. Until the beginning of your next turn, any enemy who tries to attack you must first pass a Mind Test against Tension 14. On a failure, they attack the hologram and lose the Action.

Cryptographic Sequencer: Spend 1 use before making a test to hack a system, disable an electronic lock, or decipher a coded message. You gain Advantage on that test.

Sleep Gas: Spend 1 use. ALL targets within Close distance (excluding you) must succeed on a Resistance Test against Tension 14 or gain the “Asleep” Status for 1 Round or until they suffer damage.

docs.title: MARTIAL TRAINING
docs.text:
Martial Training is divided into 3 categories: Martial Master (unarmed combat), Swordsman (melee weapons), and Marksman (ranged weapons).

Techniques: These powers work differently from the others. At Grade 1, the Hero learns 2 techniques from that Grade’s list. With each new Grade acquired, they may choose one more technique from any Grade equal to or lower than their current one. Techniques may be Active (requiring Action and/or Resolve) or Passive (permanent bonuses). Each technique also has its own Resolve cost indicated in its Grade.

docs.title: Acquiring Techniques
docs.text: To acquire techniques, a character must have the proper Grade in that Power: at Grade 1, they gain access to two techniques, and only one of those two may have the descriptor Passive. After that, each Grade grants 1 new Technique of a Grade equal to or lower than the one possessed.

docs.title: 6 PAX / Grade
docs.text: Whether with a sword, a trident, or a staff, you are a master in the use of melee weapons. To you, a weapon is an extension of your body and your will.

docs.title: Grade 1
docs.text:
Activation Cost: 1 Resolve

When acquired, choose 2 techniques (only 1 may be Passive).

docs.title: Singular Weapon
docs.text:
(Passive)

When fighting with a single type of melee weapon (swords, for example), you add your Swordsman Grade to your Attack Tests and to your Defense.

docs.title: Two-Weapon Fighting
docs.text:
(Passive)

When fighting with a melee weapon in each hand, your Multiple-attack penalty becomes –4 instead of –5.

docs.title: Sudden Charge
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You move one distance and attack in the same breath. The attack adds half your Agility bonus to the Attack Test.

docs.title: Violent Attack
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You sacrifice precision for power. Make a weapon attack, adding double your Swordsman Grade as a direct bonus to damage, but with Disadvantage on the Attack Test.

docs.title: Defensive Stance
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You focus on your defense. Your Block action gains an additional bonus equal to your Swordsman Grade.

docs.title: Precise Attack
docs.text:
(1 Action)

Make a weapon attack, adding your Damage Die as a bonus to your Attack Test.

docs.title: Grade 2
docs.text:
(Activation Cost: 2 Resolve)

When acquired, choose 1 new technique of Grade 2 or lower.

docs.title: Quick Draw
docs.text:
(Passive)

You gain a bonus to your Initiative Tests equal to your Swordsman Grade. Your first attack in each Scene gains Advantage.

docs.title: Parry Blow
docs.text:
(Reaction)

When you are the target of a melee attack, you may spend your reaction to make an Opposed Test and pit your own Attack against the enemy’s. If you win the Test, the enemy’s attack is negated.

docs.title: Arc Attack
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You make one attack that hits up to 3 adjacent enemies, each taking half your normal Damage.

docs.title: Tempest of Blows
docs.text:
(2 Actions)

You deliver three attacks in rapid succession. The Multiple-attack penalty is –2 for each of those attacks.

docs.title: 6 PAX / Grade
docs.text: You have turned your body into a living weapon. The Martial Master focuses on the use of bare hands to injure, immobilize, and stun the opponent.

docs.title: Grade 1
docs.text: Activation Cost: 1 Resolve

docs.title: Acrobatic Fighter
docs.text:
(Passive)

You add your Martial Master Grade to your Defense.

docs.title: Martial Artist
docs.text:
(Passive)

You add your Martial Master Grade to your Spirit and to your Unarmed Attack Tests.

docs.title: Brawler
docs.text:
(Passive)

You add your Martial Master Grade to your Potency and to the Damage of your Unarmed Attacks.

docs.title: Jab-Cross
docs.text:
(Passive)

Your Multiple Attack penalty becomes –4 instead of –5.

docs.title: High Guard
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You focus on your defense. Your Block action gains an additional bonus equal to your Martial Master Grade.

docs.title: Precise Strike
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You aim for an opening. Make an Unarmed Attack, adding your Damage Die as a bonus to your Attack Test.

docs.title: Grade 2
docs.text:
Activation Cost: 2 Resolve

When acquired, choose 1 new technique of Grade 2 or lower.

docs.title: Body Fortification
docs.text:
(Passive)

You add your Martial Master Grade to your Damage Reduction and to your total Resolve.

docs.title: Fists of Steel
docs.text:
(1 Action)

Your blows become as powerful as steel. Until the end of your turn, your Unarmed Attacks deal additional Damage equal to your Martial Master Grade +1.

docs.title: Acrobatic Kicks
docs.text:
(1 Action)

With a single Action, you move one distance and execute a series of kicks against a group of enemies. This attack gains a bonus to the Attack Test and to Damage equal to the number of enemies surrounding you at the end of the movement. If the enemy has the Group descriptor, you gain Advantage on the Attack Test.

docs.title: Swift Sweep
docs.text:
(1 Action)

You perform a precise sweep that causes no damage against up to 3 adjacent enemies. The Attack Test is made with –2, but all who are hit must make an Opposed Agility Test against your Potency or gain the “Prone” Status.

docs.title: 6 PAX / Grade
docs.text: Whether with bows, firearms or energy projectiles, you are a master of ranged combat. Every shot is calculated for maximum effect.

docs.title: Grade 1
docs.text:
Activation Cost: 1 Resolve

When acquired, choose 2 techniques (only 1 may be Passive).

docs.title: Favorite Weapon
docs.text:
(Passive)

Choose one type of ranged weapon (for example, Bows). When using it, you receive a bonus to your Attack Test and to Damage equal to your Marksman Grade.

docs.title: Special Ammunition
docs.text:
(Free Action)

At the beginning of your turn, you may declare that you are using special ammunition, and you have an amount of this ammunition equal to your Marksman Grade. Choose one of the following effects for your next attack:

Impact Shot: If it hits, the enemy is pushed 1 Distance.

Pinning Shot: If it hits, the enemy gains the “Slowed” Status for 1 Round.

docs.title: Ricochet Shot
docs.text:
(1 Action)

Make an attack against one target. If it hits, you may cause the projectile to ricochet and strike a second target within a Close distance of the first, who suffers half Damage.

docs.title: Grade 2
docs.text:
Activation Cost: 2 Resolve

When acquired, choose 1 new technique of Grade 2 or lower.

docs.title: Instinctive Shooter
docs.text:
(Passive)

You may make ranged attacks against Adjacent targets without suffering Disadvantage.

docs.title: Special Ammunition (Improved)
docs.text:
You add new options to your Special Ammunition ability:

  • Smoke Shot: The attack creates a small cloud of smoke at the point of impact, granting cover to the area and causing the “Blinded” Status to all who are Adjacent to the point of impact until the beginning of your next Turn or until they move away from the point of impact.

  • Boxing Glove Shot: You are able to fire boxing glove–shaped projectiles. The target must make an Opposed Resistance Test against your Accuracy. If they fail, the target suffers the “Stunned” Status until the end of the target’s next Turn.

docs.title: Barrage of Shots
docs.text:
(2 Actions)

You fire rapidly into an area. Choose one point. You make an attack against up to 3 targets within a Close distance of that point, each suffering half Damage.

docs.title: Acquiring Powers
docs.text: A Hero’s Origin defines which Powers are within their reach. In addition, each Power has each power has a PAX cost, indicated in its description. The cost refers to one Grade of that Power; for example, if a Power has a cost of 3 PAX, you must spend 6 PAX to have it at Grade 2. When you acquire a Grade in a given Power, you gain all the abilities listed at that Grade, unless otherwise specified.

docs.title: Using Powers
docs.text:
Each Power provides a set of abilities according to its Grade (see below). When a Hero acquires a Grade in that Power, they gain access to all of them. The use of these abilities requires an Activation, which is the number of Actions spent on that Power, and a Resolve Cost, which must be paid when the ability is used. Some abilities have the Passive descriptor, which indicates that they are always active.

Cost: This is the amount of Resolve spent to use a given Power. As a rule, the cost can never be reduced below 1 Resolve. Some specific abilities, such as the Champion of Tomorrow’s Classic Heroism, clearly state that there is no Resolve cost and can therefore remove the cost entirely.

Duration: Some powers create effects whose duration is given in their description; this indicates how long the power remains active. Duration may vary between Turns, Rounds, or even the entire Scene.

docs.title: Example of a Power: Force Field
docs.text:
Force Field — Name of the Power 3 PAX per Grade — Amount of PAX required to obtain that Power per Grade Grade 1 — Grade of the ability I Won’t Hold Much longer! — Name of the ability Activation: Reaction — Actions required to use the ability Cost: 1 Resolve — Resolve cost to activate the ability When you declare that your force field will not last much longer, it gains a bonus equal to twice your Grade in this Power to Defense and Damage Reduction. The Force Field is dismissed at the end of this Turn.

— Description of the ability

docs.title: GRADES
docs.text: Each Grade provides a set of abilities, and a Hero of that Grade has access to all of them. These abilities have an Activation, which indicates the number of actions spent to activate them, and a Resolve cost in their description. Some abilities are Passive, which means they do not require activation, having continuous or specific effects that happen without requiring the user to spend actions.

docs.title: Grade 1 — The Whole Neighborhood!
docs.text: Represents the most basic level of that power. A Pyrokinetic can control small flames and manipulate bonfires, a Martial Master has just completed their training, and a Speedster can cross several city blocks at an impressive speed.

docs.title: Grade 2 — The Whole City!
docs.text:
Things are starting to get more interesting.

A Grade 2 Illusionist is capable of creating illusions the size of houses, a Swordsman has enough skill to rival the greatest masters in the country, and someone with Super Strength can throw cars as if they were made of paper.

docs.title: Martial Training
docs.text: This category encompasses specialisation in many different forms of combat. Whether that be the monastic learning of traditional martial arts, military training focused on guerilla tactics and armed combat, or the mastery of a melee weapon.

docs.title: Superpowers
docs.text: This is the broadest category: everything from flying to firing beams from your eyes, metamorphosis, and even manipulating emotions. Superpowers are innate abilities or the result of a mutation; they are intrinsic to a being.

docs.title: Technology
docs.text: These are gadgets, technological armor, special weapons, and much more. Technology sufficiently advanced... well, you know the rest: anything tech and electronic, human or alien.

docs.title: SUPERPOWERS
docs.text: Whether firing beams from your eyes, controlling the elements, changing your appearance at will, or teleporting: all of these fit within the Superpowers category. As the broadest category, these are usually what we think of when imagining the concept of superheroes. This subgroup refers to the natural characteristics of a Hero. They are the result of genetic mutations or inheritance.

docs.title: 3 PAX / Grade
docs.text: You can channel the Red, the force that connects all animal life, to manifest the traits of beasts such as claws, wings, hide, and hooves. When using this power, you may manifest a number of Animal Adaptations equal to your Grade, spending 1 Resolve per activated Adaptation. These adaptations last for the Scene.

docs.title: Beast Claws
docs.text:
(Adaptation)

You manifest natural weapons. Your Damage Die increases by one step when using unarmed attacks.

docs.title: Reinforced Hide
docs.text:
(Adaptation)

Your skin becomes as thick as a rhinoceros’ hide. You gain a Defense bonus equal to your Grade in this power, +1.

docs.title: Bear Strength
docs.text:
(Adaptation)

You channel the strength of a great animal. You gain a bonus to your Potency Tests equal to your Grade+2.

docs.title: Feline Agility
docs.text:
(Adaptation)

You move with the grace of a predator. You gain Advantage on your Agility Tests.

docs.title: Eagle Wings
docs.text:
(Adaptation)

You manifest wings, gaining Flight at a Grade equal to your Grade in this power (up to a maximum of 4).

docs.title: Hunter Senses
docs.text:
(Adaptation)

Your senses sharpen. You may manifest a wolf’s sense of smell or the keen sight of an eagle, gaining Advantage on tests involving smell or sight.

docs.title: 5 PAX / Grade
docs.text: Your body has no fixed form and is completely malleable. A powerful blow would smash your head ? You flatten yourself on the spot. Is the remote control too far away to reach? You stretch your arms to grab it. The sky (or your imagination, if we are being honest) is the Limit.

docs.title: Malleable Body
docs.text:
(Passive)

You can flatten yourself to pass under doors and through cracks, and absorb damage. You gain Damage Reduction equal to your Grade in this power +1 against Physical damage.

docs.title: Extended Reach
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You are able to stretch your limbs. When doing so, you may use them to extend your reach up to Close range. You spend 1 additional Resolve point for each Round you keep Extended Reach active.

docs.title: Parachute Form
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: Resolve

You can transform into a wide, flattened shape, like a parachute or glider. You can carry a number of allies equal to your Grade in this power, +2 and safely glide from any height.

docs.title: Bounce Back
docs.text:
Activation: Reaction

Cost: 2 Resolve

When hit by an Attack, you may assume a ball-Like form, absorbing part of the impact. When doing so, you are knocked back 1 distance and take half the Damage dealt.

docs.title: Elastic Prison
docs.text:
Activation: 2 Actions

Cost: 2 Determination

You wrap an adjacent target. The target gains the “Immobilized” status and must succeed on an Opposed Potency Test against your Resistance to escape. You gain a bonus equal to your Grade in this power on the Test.

docs.title: 5 PAX / Grade
docs.text:
You are able to create, manipulate, amplify and diminish an element. Choose one element among Fire, Ice, Water, Air, Earth, Electricity, and Toxic. Each type of element must be purchased separately, and whenever you use your element for Tests, such as creating an ice ramp to save civilians or manipulating fire to reduce a blaze, you gain +2 per Grade in this power on your Tests.

When choosing this Power, decide when adding it to your sheet whether the Damage it causes is based on Potency or Spirit.

docs.title: Elemental Ray
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You make a Ranged Attack with Close range using your element. This Attack gains a bonus to hit and Damage equal to your Grade in this Power. When you achieve a Splash Page, the target gains the Status appropriate to your element:

Fire: Burned

Ice: Frozen

Earth: Immobilized Electricity: Stunned Toxic: Poisoned

docs.title: Elemental Shield
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You use your element to create a protective barrier, creating a shield that protects you and a number of allies equal to your Grade in this power, providing a bonus to Defense equal to your Grade in this Power +1. The Elemental Shield is immobile. Solid elements such as Earth and Ice provide 2 + your Grade in Defense. When an Attack hits you, the shield is dismissed.

docs.title: Elemental Propulsion
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

You use your element to propel yourself. Until the end of your next Turn, you may move 2 Distances instead of 1 with movement actions.

docs.title: Elementalize
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

You spend 2 Resolve to force the target to make an Opposed Resistance Test against your Spirit. If the target fails, it suffers the Status related to your element until the beginning of your next Turn.

Fire: Engulfed Water: Slowed Earth: Prone Air: Slowed Ice: Immobilized Electricity: Stunned Toxic: Engulfed

docs.title: 4 PAX / Grade
docs.text:
This power encompasses different forms of energy projection, such as firing lasers from the eyes, energy blasts from the hands, or even charged breath from the mouth. When you gain this power, decide whether the Damage is based on Potency or Spirit.

A Hero with this power may choose to make a simple ranged attack using their Damage Die without spending Resolve and without receiving any extra benefits from Energy Blast.

docs.title: Energy Shot
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You fire energy as a Ranged Attack. You attempt to hit an Adjacent or Close enemy with an energy blast. The Attack and Damage gain a bonus of 1 + your Grade in Energy Blast.

docs.title: Brutal Blast
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

When you hit a target with your Energy Blast, the target must make an Opposed Resistance Test against your Potency or Spirit. If they fail, the target is pushed 1 Distance.

docs.title: 3 PAX per Grade
docs.text: You possess a body more durable than normal, whether through hardened skin, metal plates, natural scales, cybernetic armor or superhuman constitution.

docs.title: Robust Body
docs.text:
Passive

Your Resistance increases by +2, and your Damage Reduction increases by +1 per Grade you possess in Enhanced Resistance.

docs.title: Brace for Impact
docs.text:
Activation: 2 Actions

Cost: 1 Resolve

You prepare yourself for an imminent impact. Until the beginning of your next turn, you may add your Enhanced Resistance Grade to your Damage Reduction against the next attack you receive.

docs.title: Superhuman Vigor
docs.text:
Passive

Your body becomes a self-sufficient and durable system. You become immune to all poisons and diseases of non-magical origin. In addition, you can hold your breath for several hours and gain resistance to environments of extreme heat and cold.

docs.title: 3 PAX / Grade
docs.text: You are capable of taking to the skies, reaching incredible speeds.

docs.title: Basic Flight
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You take flight and may move through the air. While in the air, you gain a bonus equal to your Grade in this power on your Agility Tests. For each Round after the first in which you remain airborne, you must spend 1 Resolve.

docs.title: Superhero landing
docs.text:
Passive

When you enter a combat Scene by landing from a flight, you gain a bonus to your Initiative roll equal to your Grade in Flight.

docs.title: Aerial Ride
docs.text:
Passive

You are strong enough to carry one ally with you while flying, with no penalty to speed.

docs.title: Cruising Speed
docs.text:
Passive

If you possess the Superhuman Speed power, your flight speed becomes as fast as your running speed. You may use the “Dash” movement ability from Superhuman Speed.

docs.title: 3 PAX / Grade
docs.text: You become capable of generating powerful force fields. They can be used to block attacks, as platforms, and even to imprison enemies.

docs.title: Field Generation
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action (or Reaction)

Cost: 1 Resolve

You generate a Force Field targeting yourself. It provides +2 Defense and Damage Reduction 1. The Force Field lasts for 1 Round. This ability may be used as a Reaction, as long as you are able to use it in that manner. Alternatively, you may generate the field on a target Adjacent to you.

docs.title: I Won’t Hold Much longer!
docs.text:
Activation: Reaction

Cost: 1 Resolve

When you dramatically declare that your force field will not hold much longer, it gains a bonus equal to twice your Grade in this Power to Defense and Damage Reduction. The Force Field is dismissed at the end of this Turn.

docs.title: Saving Field
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

When you use your Force Fields in Heroic Actions during Rescue Scenes, you may protect a small group of civilians, gaining a +2 bonus per Grade on Actions involving your field.

docs.title: Expanded Protection
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

Your Field Generation increases to +3 Defense and Damage Reduction 2, and may also affect 1 target within Close distance of you.

docs.title: Platform
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

Your force fields may be used as static platforms for movement and tactical positioning. You create a platform at any point you can see within a Close distance. It can support a number of targets equal to your Spirit value (minimum 1) and lasts for 1 Round.

docs.title: 12 PAX per Grade
docs.text: The Speed Force is one of the seven fundamental forces of the universe. It is the manifestation of movement and speed. Those touched by it are not mere speedsters, but true avatars of velocity: it allows incredible feats beyond simply running at absurd speeds, such as temporal manipulation, molecular vibration and even extremely accelerated thought.

docs.title: Kinetic Connection
docs.text:
Activation: Passive

Your connection to the Speed Force grants you a +3 bonus to Agility per Grade you possess in this power.

docs.title: Kinetic Impact
docs.text:
Activation: Passive

Speed is your weapon. When you spend a Movement Action before making a Melee Attack, you may use your Agility modifier instead of Potency to deal Damage.

docs.title: Accelerated Mind
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You can process information at super speed. If you have access to a data source (a book, a computer, a crime scene), you can absorb all details in a fraction of a second, gaining Advantage on your next Mind Test to analyze or learn about that subject.

docs.title: Accelerated Movement
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You may move two Distances with a single Movement Action.

docs.title: Barrage of Blows
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

You unleash a series of punches faster than the eye can see. With a single Attack roll, you strike the opponent multiple times, dealing +1 Damage Die against them.

docs.title: Instant Punch
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve You make a Melee

Attack against any target up to a Far distance away from you.

docs.title: Scarlet Tornado
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

You spin your arms or run in circles at high speed, creating a vortex of air.

Make an Attack roll against all targets within a Close distance. You deal Damage equal to half your Agility value (rounded up) to the targets. Alternatively, you may choose to pull or push the targets 1 Distance.

docs.title: Accelerated Burst
docs.text:
Activation: Free

Cost: 2 Resolve

You force yourself to go even faster, gaining +1 Movement Action that Turn or +1 Dodge. At the end of the Scene, mark one Condition.

Using the Speed Force

Although there are other powers related to speed, the Speed Force still reigns supreme. In narrative terms, a Hero (or Villain) with this power is capable of unique feats. Sweeping through an entire city in seconds, reaching the other side of the planet and returning in the same instant, the list is virtually endless.

For reasons of rules, balance, and game design in general, we could not allow a literal transcription of the Force: it would be impossible. As Narrator, adopt the principle that, following the Grade chart at the beginning of this chapter, if a user of this power thinks of a feat of speed, they can do it, as long as they succeed on a simple Test.

A character may not possess both Speed Force and Superhuman Speed under any circumstances.

docs.title: 3 PAX per Grade
docs.text:
This is a classic power that allows herculean feats of strength such as lifting heavy vehicles, removing massive debris, breaking walls with a single punch, and much more. Super

Strength is more than a simple increase to Potency; it allows its wielder to perform some extraordinary physical feats.

docs.title: Brute Strength
docs.text:
Passive

Your Potency increases by +2 per Grade in Super Strength.

docs.title: Powerful Strike
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

When you make a Melee Attack, you may activate Powerful Strike. If it hits, you roll one additional Damage Die.

docs.title: Saving Strength
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

When in Rescue Scenes and using your Super Strength in Heroic Actions, you gain Advantage on your Tests.

docs.title: 3 PAX / Grade
docs.text: You are fast. Very fast. Although not as fast as someone touched by the Speed Force, your speed still allows you to perform incredible feats of agility and momentum. A character may not possess both Superhuman Speed and Speed Force.

docs.title: Natural Runner
docs.text:
Passive

Your Agility increases by +2 per Grade you possess in Superhuman Speed.

docs.title: Dash
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

While in contact with the ground, you may concentrate your speed into a single burst, moving faster than the eye can follow. You may move up to two Distances instead of one.

docs.title: Quick Reflexes
docs.text:
Passive

Your reflexes are enhanced, allowing you to react to danger before most people even realize it exists. You add your Grade in Superhuman Speed to your Initiative rolls.

docs.title: 5 PAX/Grade
docs.text: You can bend space or pierce dimensions to travel from point A to point B instantaneously, ignoring any physical barriers between them.

docs.title: Spatial Sense
docs.text:
Activation: Passive

Your brain processes space at hyper-accelerated speed so you don’t appear inside a wall.

You receive a bonus equal to your Grade in this Power on Agility checks that involve moving and jumping. Additionally, you receive a Bonus on your Defense equal to your Grade in this Power, +1.

docs.title: Tactical Jump
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You “blink” in space, teleporting yourself to any point you can see within Near range. On Rescue Scenes, you ignore any difficult terrain, chasms, or high walls, you don’t need to roll to reach victims in precarious locations (like the top of a burning building or a cliff), you simply appear there.

docs.title: Space Warp
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You use teleport to instantly flank and teleport to a space Adjacent to an enemy, performing a Melee Attack in the same movement with Advantage.

docs.title: Quick Extraction
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

You touch an ally, civilian, or object (up to the size of a motorcycle) and leap through space with it to any Distant point. If you attempt to teleport an enemy, make an Opposed Agility Test against the Potency or Agility of the target whichever is higher.

docs.title: Evasive Teleport
docs.text:
Activation: Reactio

Cost: 2 Resolve

When you are targeted by an attack (melee or ranged), you can disappear one millisecond before impact and add your Teleportation Grade to your Block or Dodge against that Attack. If the attack misses, you reappear at any point within Near range.

docs.title: TECHNOLOGY
docs.text:
Technology sufficiently advanced is as impactful as any superpower. In the universe of JLU RPG, it can equal or surpass superhuman abilities. Imagine a technological armor capable of rivalling Kryptonian strength, running on the most sophisticated quantum computers, and bearing weapons with as much firepower as any optical blast.

Technologies are powerful pieces of equipment that provide many different capabilities to their users: in a connected world, someone with access to the right devices can influence global events, neutralize gigantic threats and simulate powers possessed only by the most extraordinary beings. From the Dark Knight who uses Technological Spheres to investigate a crime scene to the Genius who uses an Exoskeleton to fly at rocket speed, technology is a powerful front.

docs.title: 8 PAX / Grade
docs.text:
This armor (yes, mechanically the Exoskeleton counts as armor) enhances the abilities of whoever wears it, transforming an ordinary person into a one-man army. When you acquire this power, you build your Exoskeleton by choosing two Improvements from the list below. With each new Grade, you may add one more Improvement*.

The use of these abilities is covered by the normal Action cost, unless otherwise specified. The activation cost is 1 Resolve for Grade 1; 2 for Grade 2; 4 for Grade 3; 6 for Grade 4; and 8 for Grade 5.

If your Resolve reaches 0, your armor enters emergency mode, disabling all of its Improvements until it is recharged.

docs.title: Strength Systems
docs.text:
(Passive)

Powerful servomotors increase your strength. At Grade 1, your Potency becomes 10. For each subsequent Grade, gain +3 Potency.

docs.title: Integrated Weaponry
docs.text:
(Passive)

Your suit has an integrated weapons system. You gain the benefits of the Energy Blast power at a Grade equal to your Exoskeleton Grade.

Using Energy Blast costs 1 Action and the Resolve cost corresponding to the Grade used.

docs.title: Flight Thrusters
docs.text:
(Passive)

Your armor has a flight system. You gain the Flight power at a Grade equal to your Exoskeleton Grade.

docs.title: Force Field Generator
docs.text:
(Passive)

The suit can project an energy barrier. You gain the Force Field power at a Grade equal to your Exoskeleton Grade. Using Force Field costs 1 Action and the Resolve cost corresponding to the Grade used.

docs.title: Composite Armor
docs.text:
(Passive)

The armor is made from an ultra-resistant alloy. You gain a permanent +1 Defense per Grade in Exoskeleton and Damage Reduction 2.

docs.title: Sensor Package
docs.text:
(Passive)

A set of advanced sensors is integrated into your helmet. You gain the Special Senses power (of your choice) at a Grade equal to your Exoskeleton Grade. Using Special Senses costs 1 Action and the Resolve cost corresponding to the Grade used.

docs.title: Sealed Suit
docs.text:
(Passive)

The armor is sealed, allowing you to operate in any environment. You can breathe in a vacuum or underwater, and become immune to damage from extreme heat/cold and to the Burned and Frozen Statuses.

docs.title: Onboard Computer
docs.text:
(Passive)

The suit possesses a tactical A.I. While wearing the armor, you gain the Tech Knowledge.

docs.title: 4 PAX/Grade
docs.text:
You are accompanied by a set of high-tech spherical drones that respond to your commands, acting as your eyes, shields, weapons, and loyal companions. The spheres possess Functions, And you can have a number of active Functions equal to your Grade in that Power. Each one has an Activation and a Cost, as well as a duration, specified in its description.

Identical Functions do not stack. If your Resolve reaches zero, the Spheres are deactivated.

docs.title: Defense Mode
docs.text:
Activation: Free

Cost: 2 Resolve

The spheres orbit around you at high speed, intercepting attacks. By the end of the Scene, you receive a bonus to your Defense equal to your Grade in this Power.

docs.title: Attack Mode
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

The spheres position themselves for combat, opening their energy emitters. By the end of the Scene, you gain access to the power. Energy Blast with a Grade equal to your Grade in this Power.

docs.title: Propulsion Mode
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 2 Resolve

The spheres attach themselves to you, functioning as a propulsion system. You receive the power. Flight (Grade 1) until the end of the Scene.

docs.title: Electromagnetic Pulse
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 3 Resolve

The spheres release a pulse that disables nearby technology. Robotic enemies or those with armor that generate technological effects, such as the Exoskeleton, must make a Test of Resistance (Tension 16) or lose access to their technological abilities for 1 Round.

docs.title: Tactical Analysis
docs.text:
Activation: 1 Action

Cost: 1 Resolve

You control the spheres to scan the area. Until the end of the Scene, you receive Advantage on your next Test of Mind to search for clues, hidden enemies, or technological anomalies in the Zone.

docs.title: ARCHETYPES
docs.text:
Each Archetype grants access to unique traits and special abilities that reflect its philosophy. Think of it as the ‘why’ behind your superheroics, the motivation that drives your Hero to act. Choose carefully, because your Archetype will guide the way you interact with the world and the way the world reacts to you.

When you choose your Archetype, at Tier D you gain two abilities from it.

docs.title: Champion of Tomorrow
docs.text:
You carry hope wherever you go. As the Champion of Tomorrow, your presence inspires civilians, motivates allies, and makes villains hesitate. The community expects great things from you and the eyes of the world are always upon you. Be the beacon in the darkness and a symbol of justice.

Examples: Superman, Black Lightning and Wonder Woman.

docs.title: Code of Conduct
docs.text:
The Champion of Tomorrow’s Code of Conduct is what guides your heroism. This code is your compass and if you break it, you lose all of your Resolve points. Choose one of the options below:

Set the Example: You do not use excessive force in the fight against villainy. Whenever you leave a villain Wounded, you must offer them a chance to surrender.

Render Unto Caesar: You follow the law of humankind and may not place yourself above justice. You must always obey the law and follow lawful orders.

Protection: You must always prioritize the rescue of innocents. As long as people are in danger in the game, you must save them before doing anything else.

docs.title: Champion of Tomorrow Archetype Abilities
docs.text:
Inspiring Presence

Once per Round, if your allies can see or hear you, you may spend 3 Resolve to inspire them. ALL allies gain a bonus equal to your Tier on their next roll.

No One Gets left Behind!

Once per Scene, when an ally or civilian would suffer Damage, you may instantly move to them, intercepting the blow or hazard that would harm them and taking the Damage in their place. Regardless of the amount of Damage, you mark one Condition.

Classic Heroism

In a Rescue Scene, you do not spend Resolve when taking your first action. This ability ignores the rule that every Activation must cost at least 1 Resolve.

Truth and Justice

You have a nose for lies and corruption. Once per Scene, you may spend 4 Resolve to count as having scored an automatic success on Tests involving revealing the truth, exposing the unseen, or uncovering corruption.

docs.title: Dark Knight
docs.text:
You have learned to use shadows and darkness to your advantage. As a shadowy vigilante, you fight in the night using stealth tactics, martial arts and specialized gear. Perhaps you are a member of the Bat-Family, or perhaps you come from a lineage of shadow assassins. Either way, you are fast, precise and deadly.

Examples: Nightwing, Batman and Midnighter.

docs.title: Feet on the Ground
docs.text: While others fly, shoot beams from their eyes, and command the elements, you have other ways of fighting villainy. The only Powers a Dark Knight may have above Grade 1 are Martial Training and Technology.

docs.title: Dark Knight Archetype Abilities
docs.text:
I Am the Night

Once per Scene, as long as no one is looking at you and you are not restrained or prevented from moving, you may disappear and reappear in another adjacent Zone.

Martial Artist

You gain Grade 1 in Martial Training.

Utility Belt

You have a belt with exactly the right gear for any situation. Need to reach the top of a building quickly? You have a grappling gun. Need to lose your enemies? Smoke bomb them. Once per Scene, you may spend 3 Resolve to gain a suitable item that helps you overcome a challenge narratively (night-vision goggles, a grappling line, a gas mask and so on).

Prep Time

You possess special training, a contingency plan, or some other extremely useful skill that helps you at the last possible moment. Once per Issue, when you use your Prep Time, you gain 1 Plot Point.

docs.title: Genius
docs.text:
In a world of powerful aliens and capricious deities, you know that the mind is the most powerful weapon of all. Your brilliant intellect has taken you to places that even the most fantastic powers could not. You know that planning is essential to action and having an ace up your sleeve never hurts.

Examples: Mr. Terrific, The Atom, and Lex Luthor.

docs.title: Overthinking
docs.text: Sometimes you freeze while considering the countless possible outcomes. You suffer Disadvantage on your Initiative rolls.

docs.title: Genius Archetype Abilities
docs.text:
Checkmate

Everything is clear, like a chessboard. Once per Scene, you may spend 1 Action to move an ally who is within the same Zone as you. You may move them out of danger, place them strategically between yourself and an opponent, or simply put them in the perfect position for an attack.

It’s Trivial!

Whenever you come across an artifact, device, vehicle or something similar, you automatically understand the basics of how it works. Given enough time, you can also repair any kind of mechanism created on Earth.

Technological Knowledge

You gain 1 Grade in a Technology Power.

Blabblalogy

Once per Issue, when you encounter advanced technology, an ancient tale, a strange substance or something similar, you may launch into an extended scientific explanation. When you do, you gain 1 Plot Point.

docs.title: Enraged
docs.text:
Raw, concentrated power, charging at the enemy like a true wrecking ball on the battlefield. The Enraged is a living weapon of war, ready to go all out and unleash all of their fury.

Examples: Big Barda, Kilowog, and Hawkman.

docs.title: Collateral Damage
docs.text: You hit first and ask questions later. In a Scene, you cannot help civilians until the threat has been completely neutralized.

docs.title: Enraged Archetype Abilities
docs.text:
Everything in the Ring

Choose one enemy who is fighting you. Until the end of the Scene, whenever the two of you fight each other, both of you gain Advantage on Attack and Damage rolls.

Chain Breaker

You can tear through structures as though they were nothing. Once per Scene, spend 2 Resolve to break a barrier, such as a steel gate, mystical bindings or reinforced walls.

Red with Rage

Once per Scene, when you mark Wounded, you gain a bonus equal to your Tier +2 on your Attack and Damage rolls until the end of the Scene or until you recover from that Condition.

Cardboard World

Once per Issue, when you face a situation in which you can unleash the full extent of your powers—such as a powerful enemy or an almost insurmountable obstacle, deliver a speech about how you no longer need to hold back. Your Damage Die increases by one step until the end of the Scene.

docs.title: ORIGIN
docs.text:
A Hero’s Origin represents their starting point. It is a combination of biology, culture, and upbringing. Perhaps they came from a distant planet that was destroyed, were created in a laboratory or descended from a noble lineage beneath the ocean.

Power Kit: Each Origin offers Heroes a unique list of predefined powers, called a Power Kit. During Hero creation, the player may choose one Grade in a Power from that Kit for free.

Buying Other Powers: Can a Kryptonian master electric powers? Can an Amazon be touched by the Speed Force? Yes. Although uncommon, it is not impossible for a Hero to gain powers that are not typical of their Origin. Whenever this happens, the power costs double the PAX per Grade. Humans are the exception to this rule and cannot buy any powers from outside of their Power Kit.

docs.title: Amazon
docs.text: Fueling countless legends, the Amazons are a civilization of female warriors originating from the island of Themyscira, with roots in ancient Greece. Raised by the gods of the Olympian pantheon, Amazons are trained from a young age in the arts of war and strategy, such as archery, swordsmanship, and hand-to-hand combat.

docs.title: Amazon Origin Powers Kit
docs.text:
• Super Strength

  • Enhanced Resistance

  • Superhuman Speed

  • Combat Training

docs.title: Amazon Equipment
docs.text: You receive an Amazon Armor that grants you DR equals your Tier+1, and an Amazon Sword that grants you +2 on your Attack rolls and +1 in Damage.

docs.title: Divine longevity
docs.text: Amazons are beings created by deities, and can live forever if they are not harmed. Every Amazon receives the Perennial Trait.

docs.title: Sisters in Arms
docs.text: You receive the Affiliation (Themyscira) Trait.

docs.title: Perennial (Trait)
docs.text:
Time has no power over you. Whether by divine blessing, a scientific accident, or your unique biology, your body has stopped aging. You are immune to its effects. It is a natural process and one cannot die of old age.

I remember that!: Once per Issue, when you come across a historical figure, event, or culture, you can state that you remember it. The Editor will tell you an important fact about that figure.

docs.title: Human Power Kit
docs.text:
• Martial Training

  • Technology

docs.title: Only Human
docs.text: Humans cannot purchase Powers outside their Power Kit.

docs.title: Versatility
docs.text: Your Hero gains one Knowledge and one Simple Trait.

docs.title: Kryptonian Origin Power Kit
docs.text:
• Energy Blast

  • Invulnerability

  • Enhanced Resistance

  • Enhanced Senses

  • Super Strength

  • Super-Breath

  • Superhuman Speed

  • Flight

docs.title: Blood of Krypton
docs.text: You gain a bonus to Potency and Damage Reduction equal to your Tier. Whenever your Tier increases, both the bonus and the Damage Reduction increase as well.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: When exposed to green Kryptonite, Kryptonians lose access to all their powers and become Vulnerable. Unless they are under the effects of a yellow sun, Kryptonians lose their Powers.

docs.title: Meta-Human
docs.text: Meta-Humans are individuals who possess the meta-gene, a mutation capable of granting its bearer a vast range of abilities. Since no two meta-genes are alike, the variety of powers available to Meta-Humans is virtually limitless. They come in all types, shapes, and sizes, and are most commonly found on planet Earth.

docs.title: Meta-Human Power Kit
docs.text: Meta-Humans do not receive a free Power. Instead, they may purchase any Superpower at its normal cost.

docs.title: CHARACTER CREATION IN BRIEF: THE SEVEN STEPS
docs.text:
Define the Tier: Tier defines the scope of a Hero. In this quickstart, we provide Tier D and Tier C.

Choose an Origin: A Hero’s Origin is a combination of culture, biology and sometimes the source of their power. Choose between Human, Kryptonian, or Meta-Human.

Choose an Archetype: An Archetype is a comic book trope that a Hero follows: the ones provided in this quickstart are Champion of Tomorrow, Dark Knight, Genius and Enraged

Distribute the Attributes: Assign your Hero’s basic talents: Potency, Accuracy, Agility, Resistance, Spirit and Mind.

Tier PAX Resolve Defense Attack Bonus Damage Die Attribute Limit Power Limit D – Year One 40 12 15 +1 1d6 +6 Grade 2 C – Local Hero 60 15 18 +2 1d6 +9 Grade 2

Choose your Powers: Your tools for fighting evil.

Determine Knowledge and Traits: Knowledge represents acquired expertise, while Traits are unique qualities possessed by your Hero.

Final Details: Your Hero’s name, weakness and soul.

docs.title: HERO TIER
docs.text:
Tier determines a Hero’s level. Wonder Woman is not on the same level as Wonder Girl, even though both possess similar abilities. Tier defines a Hero’s Attributes, available PAX, Resolve, combat values such as Defense, Damage Die, and Attack Bonus, as well as the maximum Limit for an Attribute’s value.

Tier: Some abilities indicate that you should use a bonus equal to your Tier. In this case, in ascending order, treat Tier D as the starting point, with a value of 1, and Tier S as the final point, with a value of 5. As for Tier E the value is zero.

Tier also imposes Limits on a Hero’s Attributes and Powers. In the case of the Attribute Limit, this refers to values purchased directly through PAX. However, this Limit can be exceeded through certain Powers. For example, if a Tier D Hero spends 10 PAX to reach +6 Potency, they may still go beyond that value if they possess Super Strength. In the case of the Power Limit, it means that only one Power may have the listed Grade, while all other Powers must remain at a lower Grade.

docs.title: PAX
docs.text:
PAX represents a Hero’s full potential. They are the means through which a Hero purchases and improves various abilities. Players may be awarded Ascension Points during or at the end of a game session. PAX are the currency used to buy powers, knowledge, traits and other details for your Hero.

Advancement Cost Attribute Increase 5 PAX for each +3 Power Purchase Variable Traits 4 to 12 PAX Knowledge 4 PAX Increase Resolve 2 PAX for each 1 point

docs.title: ATTRIBUTES
docs.text: Attributes are represented by numerical values in ascending order. If a Hero has +3 Mind, they are not as intelligent as one who has +9 in that same Attribute. For Heroes, Attributes increase in multiples of 3. Each Attribute increase costs 5 PAX. Although Attributes are expressed as modifiers, their representation and capabilities are entirely narrative, depending on the creativity of the player using them and the permission granted by the Editor for the Scene.

docs.title: Potency
docs.text:
Potency Tests can be used for:

Feats of Strength: Lifting a bus to save a trapped civilian, holding up a collapsing bridge beam, or hurling a car at an opponent.

Destruction: Forcing open a reinforced steel door, breaking handcuffs, or punching a hole through a concrete wall.

Physical Intimidation: Using your size and strength to coerce a henchman into talking, without necessarily throwing a punch.

docs.title: Accuracy
docs.text:
Accuracy Tests can be used for:

Attacks: Striking an opponent directly, whether by landing a punch or firing a projectile.

Delicate Tasks: Disarming the trigger of an apocalyptic device, performing field microsurgery, or disabling an alarm without setting it off.

Sleight of Hand: Hiding an important object in the palm of your hand or planting a tracking device on a target without them noticing.

docs.title: Agility
docs.text:
Agility Tests can be used for:

Dodging: Avoiding a hail of bullets, leaping away from an explosion, or evading an enemy’s strike.

Acrobatics: Running along the side of a skyscraper, leaping between rooftops, balancing on a narrow surface, or contorting yourself to escape restraints.

Stealth: Moving silently to avoid detection by guards or sneaking through an enemy base.

Initiative: Reacting faster than your opponents at the start of a combat or crisis scene.

docs.title: Resistance
docs.text:
Resistance Tests can be used for:

Enduring Hardships: Surviving days of travel through a desert, holding your breath for long periods underwater, or resisting extreme heat or cold.

Resisting Harmful Effects: Fighting off the effects of the Joker’s poison gas, resisting disease or enduring exposure to radiation.

Absorbing Impact: Withstanding the force of a great fall or the punch of a super-strong enemy, reducing its effects.

Maintaining Concentration: Keeping a power or spell active even while taking damage.

docs.title: Spirit
docs.text:
Spirit Tests can be used for:

Willpower: Resisting torture, Gorilla Grodd’s mind control or fear-inducing illusions.

Social Presence: Calming a panicked crowd, persuading a guard to let you pass, deceiving a villain or inspiring your teammates to keep fighting.

Magic: Channeling mystical energy to cast a spell or communicating with astral entities.

Intuition: Having a gut feeling about a trap, sensing someone’s true intentions behind their words or feeling a supernatural presence.

docs.title: Mind
docs.text:
Mind Tests can be used for:

Investigation: Searching for clues at a crime scene, noticing something out of place in a room or following a complex trail.

Knowledge: Recalling a crucial fact about ancient history, identifying the chemical composition of a substance, or remembering the weakness of a mythological enemy.

Tactics and Strategy: Deducing the next step in a villain’s plan, finding the best infiltration route into an enemy base, or coordinating a team attack.

docs.title: STATUS
docs.text: Some abilities may cause a wide variety of effects in a Hero. Unlike Conditions, Heroes do not have a Limit on the number of Statuses they can receive, but two identical Statuses do not stack.

docs.title: Shaken
docs.text: Makes any Mind or Spirit test with Disadvantage.

docs.title: Asleep
docs.text: Cannot perform actions. If they suffer any type of Damage, they wake immediately.

docs.title: Frightened
docs.text: Suffers Disadvantage on all tests against the source of fear, and cannot willingly move closer to it.

docs.title: Stunned
docs.text: Loses 1 Action on their turn.

docs.title: Prone
docs.text:
The character must spend 1 Movement Action to stand or regain their footing before they can use any more Movement Actions.

While Prone:

  • They cannot move.

  • They make all attacks (melee and ranged) with Disadvantage.

docs.title: Blinded
docs.text: Suffers Disadvantage on all actions that depend on sight.

docs.title: Frozen
docs.text: Is Immobilized and suffers 1 Damage per Round.

docs.title: Confused
docs.text:
At the start of the turn, roll 1d6:

  • 1 to 4: Attacks the nearest ally with all available actions.

  • 5 to 6: Acts normally, but all actions cost double Resolve.

docs.title: Controlled
docs.text: Is under the control of another character. During their turn, whoever controls them chooses their actions.

docs.title: Weakened
docs.text: Disadvantage on Potency Tests.

docs.title: Poisoned
docs.text: Is Engulfed in poison. Suffers the effects of Engulfed (see below).

docs.title: Engulfed
docs.text: Suffers 2 Damage per Round due to poison, flames, bleeding, or another ongoing effect.

docs.title: Exhausted
docs.text:
Cannot recover Resolve through rest or abilities.

Suffers Disadvantage on all Potency, Resistance, and Mind tests.

docs.title: Immobilized
docs.text: Cannot move. May act normally, as long as movement is not required. May attempt to break free.

docs.title: Slowed
docs.text: ALL Movement Actions cost +1 additional Action.

docs.title: Burned
docs.text: Is Engulfed in flames. Suffers the effects of Engulfed.

docs.title: Bleeding
docs.text: Loses 2 Resolve per Tier at the start of each turn.

docs.title: Vulnerable
docs.text: Has no Resolve. Any amount of Damage causes them to mark a Condition Box.

docs.title: MOVEMENT
docs.text: Knowing how to position yourself can be the difference between the success and failure of a mission. In a setting with runners capable of surpassing the speed of light, artifacts that teleport in the blink of an eye, acrobatic fighters and warriors who fly with metal wings, movement is essential.

docs.title: Zone
docs.text: A Zone is the area where the action is taking place. An abandoned factory, a laboratory complex, the skies of Metropolis, or anything similar: it represents the place where everything is happening. It is not uncommon for there to be several Zones in a Scene, if the characters are fighting through the skies of the City of Tomorrow, they are in one Zone, while the Daily Planet building below them may be considered another distinct one.

docs.title: Distances
docs.text:
Even in an abstract way, it is still important to define distances within the same Zone. The distances are Adjacent, Close, Far, and Distant.

Adjacent: Within arm’s reach, generally engaged in melee combat. It is not necessary to spend movement actions to interact with a target that is Adjacent.

Close: Nearby, a few steps or leaps away. It is necessary to spend one movement action to bring a Close target to an Adjacent distance.

Far: Still visible, but requires a greater effort to get there. It is necessary to spend two movement actions to bring a Far target to an Adjacent distance.

Distant: Practically at the other end of a Zone. It is necessary to spend three movement actions to bring a Distant target to an Adjacent distance.

Target Distance Actions Required Adjacent 0 Close 1 Far 2 Distant 3

Powers such as Super Speed or Speed Force usually reduce the need to spend movement actions to reach an Adjacent distance from the target.

Ranged attacks, such as Energy Beams, thrown objects, and firearms, reach targets at different distances. Higher-Grade Powers can reach farther, as can more modern weapons and advanced technologies.

docs.title: COMBAT ACTIONS
docs.text:
During combat, each character has 3 Actions in a Round. These include Attacks, movement, the use of powers and strategic assistance.
